Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
 Office Notes, reports,
 orders or proceedings
Sl.
 Date or directions and Court'S Or Judges'S Order

S No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  CRLA No. 421 of 2019  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Ms. Anmol Sandhu, learned counsel holding the brief of Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. This is an admitted appeal, admitted on 29.08.2019 and the Trial Court record were also summoned.
Now, the paper book is also ready and supplied to the learned counsel for the parties.

4. Heard on the bail application (CRMA No. 2509 of 2019).
5.

The present appellant- Laxman Kashyap has been convicted by the F.T.C./Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO), Haldwani, District Nainital by judgment and order dated 22.07.2019 passed in Special Session Trial No. 22 of 2017 for the offences punishable under Section 376(2) of IPC

entities.text: F.T.C./Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO), Haldwani, District Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: with the sentence of 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 20,000/- and in default of payment of fine it is further provided that he has to undergo further six months additional imprisonment.

In addition to this, the appellant has also been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 313 IPC with 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 15,000/- and in default of payment of fine he has to further undergo four months additional simple imprisonment.
Both the sentences shall run concurrently.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has already served more than half of the sentence and have no previous criminal history.
CRLA/421/2019 on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172541137/
1 7.
On instructions, learned State counsel informs to this court that the appellant has already served 6 years 10 months without remission and is in long incarceration.

8. After hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration that the appellant have already completed more than half of the sentence, this court is of the view that the appellant deserves for bail, accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, bail application is allowed.

9. Let the appellant/applicant-Laxman Kashyap be released on bail during the pendency of the instant criminal appeal on furnishing his personal bond and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
Realisation of fine shall remain suspended.
10. List this matter for final hearing in the month of May, 2025.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 10.12.2024 PR CRLA/421/2019 on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172541137/
2
